re_line: Trump-Xi summit outcomes, Taiwan arms package on hold, Second Thomas Shoal standoff, China's aid to Iran, Chinese tech curbs in Congress
editors_note: Ceremony in Washington left export controls, AI and Taiwan arms sales unresolved, while friction at sea, over Iran and over military technology kept building beneath it.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Golden Week ends with fuel export approvals in focus
week_at_a_glance.body: China's seven-day National Day holiday concludes on October 7, and traders are watching whether Beijing resumes approvals for refiners' fuel exports suspended for the break. Reuters reported that Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and that PetroChina cancelled a small number of planned gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes on September 30.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson and Wicker back stalled Taiwan arms package
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed suggestions that a delayed $14 billion Taiwan arms package is being used as leverage in trade talks, the Taipei Times reported, and said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across two terms. Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker said U.S. security commitments to Taiwan must be upheld after meeting Taiwan's representative Alexander Yui. Four other Republican senators called on the administration to release more than $14 billion in stalled Taiwan security assistance.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate delays Chinese car ban until after midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate punted a bill that would permanently ban Chinese-made cars from the U.S. market until after the November 3 midterm elections, AP reported. Senators plan to bring the measure up again for a vote in November.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate optical module ban proposal hits Chinese stocks
heard_on_the_hill.body: The ChiNext index dropped 4.53 percent and the SSE Composite fell 3.2 percent to a one-year low on September 28 as a proposed Senate ban on Chinese optical modules in national-security systems weighed on sentiment, Bloomberg reported. The bipartisan bill includes a five-year grace period, according to Jiemian.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Lawmakers move to bar Chinese datacenter technology
heard_on_the_hill.body: Members of Congress are moving to keep Chinese-origin datacenter hardware and software out of sensitive U.S. government systems, Reuters reported, following warnings that Chinese AI models and cloud infrastructure could pose data-security risks to federal networks.
heard_on_the_hill.event: Chinese datacenter technology push in Congress

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Moreno says his vehicle bill would spare Mercedes-Benz
heard_on_the_hill.body: Sen. Moreno said a bill he is sponsoring to bar companies with more than 15 percent Chinese ownership from selling vehicles in the U.S. would not affect Mercedes-Benz, CNBC reported.

in_the_news.headline: Divisions between US and China 'simmer beneath the surface' after Xi's Washington visit
in_the_news.body: Xi Jinping's September 23-25 state visit to Washington produced an eight-point consensus, including more favorable tariff treatment on $30 billion of goods each way and a November AI dialogue, AP reported. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the tariff truce was extended by two months. The New York Times reported that export controls, AI and Taiwan arms sales went unaddressed in public readouts.

in_the_news.headline: Philippines accuses China of obstructing resupply mission
in_the_news.body: The Philippines accused China of obstructing a resupply mission in the South China Sea, Reuters reported; Bloomberg, cited by HKEJ, said the September 24 mission to Manila's grounded vessel at Second Thomas Shoal was the first such incident since 2024. The U.S. embassy in Manila accused Beijing of "dangerous blocking and irresponsible manoeuvres." On September 27 the PLA and China Coast Guard ran joint drills around Scarborough Shoal.

in_the_news.headline: Trump told Xi Chinese support for Iran 'unacceptable,' received assurances, US envoy says
in_the_news.body: Satellite imagery and intelligence support from Chinese groups has helped Iran strike U.S. military bases with improved precision, according to U.S. intelligence assessments described to CNN by four sources. Ambassador David Perdue said Trump told Xi at the summit that Chinese assistance to Iran was "totally unacceptable" and received assurances.

in_the_news.event: F-35 parts diverted to Hong Kong
in_the_news.headline: F-35 parts diverted to Hong Kong shipped via UPS route that often transits China
in_the_news.body: F-35 parts were diverted to Hong Kong via a UPS route that regularly passes through China, Bloomberg reported, prompting scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers. The stealth-coated canopy and weapons-bay-door components came from an Australian F-35, and the Chinese government has taken possession and not returned them, the Taipei Times reported. The F-35 Joint Program Office confirmed a "shipment issue."

in_the_news.headline: DeepSeek and Huawei unveil AI chip tools to rival Nvidia's software stack
in_the_news.body: DeepSeek and Huawei have jointly developed software tools for advanced AI chips to give Chinese developers an alternative to Nvidia's chip-software ecosystem, the New York Times reported. The push is part of Beijing's AI self-reliance drive following U.S. restrictions on Nvidia's most advanced chips.

research_roundup.headline: The Limits of Trump and Xi’s Photo-Op Summit
research_roundup.body: David Sacks of CFR argues the visit may have set "a new high-water mark for symbolism and a new low for substance," with no consensus on major geopolitical issues, AI or the economic relationship. The only clear winner, he writes, was Zoo Atlanta.

research_roundup.headline: The Trump-Xi Summit Leaves Taiwan in Limbo
research_roundup.body: CNAS finds that public accounts of the summit show no U.S. agreement to Xi's push on Taiwan, and argues that whether Trump can keep negotiating with Xi while making Taiwan harder to conquer "is now the measure of his cross-Strait policy."

research_roundup.headline: How do we deal with Chinese overcapacity?
research_roundup.body: Cecilia Malmström, Yeling Tan, Alicia García-Herrero and Nicolas Lamp take up Chinese overcapacity after a summit that produced no agreement on it, noting that an EU-China working group on "macroeconomic imbalances" set up in May has failed to produce results.

research_roundup.headline: The PRC’s Compute Push Goes Global
research_roundup.body: Dennis Yang of the Jamestown Foundation finds Beijing laying the groundwork to export computing power abroad even as U.S. export controls leave Chinese firms in a compute crunch, citing Shenzhen's AI action plan released in early September.

research_roundup.headline: A paradoxical purge: Xi shows his power, and his trouble in controlling the PLA
research_roundup.body: Michael Clarke and Jade Guan of ASPI argue the expulsions of Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli reveal both the reach of the party's disciplinary apparatus and the persistence of disloyalty and corruption in the PLA.
